extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys/agents), USPTO examiners and staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for pre-grant publication, redacted publication, notices of foreign filing, express abandonment to avoid publication, petitions to revive abandoned applications, republication and corrected publication under USPTO/MPEP and relevant CFR/USC provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of foreign filing within 45 days (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure of the applicant to provide the required notice of foreign filing within 45 days of the subsequent filing of a counterpart application shall result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If at the time the foreign filing is made the applicant still has an operative nonpublication request, a notice of foreign filing must be made within 45 days of the foreign filing or the U.S. application with the nonpublication request will become abandoned. The benefit of a certificate of mailing or transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 will be given to a notice of foreign filing. If the end of the 45 day period falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, filing on the next succeeding secular or business day is timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PTO/SB/36 may be used to rescind nonpublication and give notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/36 (revision April 2001 or later) may be used both to rescind a nonpublication request and provide notice of foreign filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/36 includes a certificate of mailing. The form is reproduced in MPEP § 1135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of abandoned application for unintentional delay (37 CFR 1.137)
rubrics_metrics.description: An abandoned application may be revived on the basis of unintentional delay by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantable petition must be accompanied by: (1) the reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(m); (3) any terminal disclaimer (and fee per § 1.20(d)) required by paragraph (d); and (4) a statement that the entire delay from the due date until filing of the petition was unintentional. The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirements for revival (37 CFR 1.137(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must include the required reply appropriate to the reason for abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: In an application abandoned under § 1.57(a), the reply must include a copy of the specification and any drawings of the previously filed application. If abandoned for failure to pay the issue fee or publication fee, the reply must include payment. For nonprovisional applications abandoned for failure to prosecute, filing a continuing application may meet the reply requirement; for certain nonprovisional applications abandoned after close of prosecution the reply may be met by filing an RCE in compliance with § 1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival for abandonment due to failure to notify of foreign filing (37 CFR 1.137(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application abandoned pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii) for failure to timely notify the Office of a foreign filing may be revived only pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply requirement of paragraph (c) is met by the notification of such foreign filing, but filing the petition will not operate to stay any period for reply that may be running against the application. Form PTO/SB/64a may be used for such a petition to revive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory abandonment may occur without Office recognition; remedy is petition to revive
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment occurs by operation of statute, and the Office may be unaware when applicant has filed a counterpart foreign application contrary to their certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant failed to file the required notice, prosecution may continue and the application may issue as a patent even though abandoned by operation of statute. Applicants who determine a required notice was not timely provided should promptly file a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137; the reply requirement is met by the notification but revival does not stay other reply periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment to avoid publication (37 CFR 1.138(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking to abandon an application to avoid publication must submit a declaration of express abandonment by way of a petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) including the fee in § 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such petition and declaration must be filed in sufficient time to permit officials to recognize the abandonment and remove the application from the publication process. Applicants should expect petitions will not be granted unless received more than four weeks prior to the projected publication date. The Office cannot ensure removal from publication any time after the publication process is initiated (about 4 months prior to projected publication date). Forms PTO/AIA/24A (for apps filed on/after Sep 16, 2012) or PTO/SB/24A (before Sep 16, 2012) may be used. Electronic filing increases the chances of timely recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee payment timing and consequences (37 CFR 1.211(e), 1.18(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication fee must be paid in each application published under § 1.211 before a patent will be granted; the fee specified in the Notice of Allowance must be paid within three months from mailing of the notice to avoid abandonment; the three-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is not published under this section the publication fee (if paid) will be refunded. The small entity discount is not available for the publication fee. Applicant may file a refund request after 4 weeks from the issue date if the application did not publish. If an RCE is filed after a Notice of Allowance but before expiration of the three-month period, the Office will suspend the due date for the publication fee until three months from mailing of the new Notice of Allowance. Effective Jan 1, 2014 the publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d) is $0.00 (per this MPEP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Publication and notifications of date changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will be informed of the projected publication date on the filing receipt; the Office will mail a 'Notice of Publication' when the application is published but not a paper copy of the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'Notice of New or Revised Publication Date' may be mailed if the publication date changes by more than six weeks due to processing delays, if a secrecy order is removed, or subsequent to revival of an abandoned application. If applicant timely corrects benefit or priority claims before technical preparation begins, the Office will mail a corrected filing receipt informing applicant of the newly assigned projected publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and public availability of applications (37 CFR 1.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that have not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) are generally preserved in confidence pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(a); information will only be given to the public as set forth in § 1.11 or § 1.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published abandoned applications and published pending applications are available to the public as set forth in § 1.11(a) and § 1.14(a)(1)(ii)/(iii) upon request and payment of the fee in § 1.19(b). If a redacted copy was used for publication, copies provided may be limited to the redacted copy. The Office may, at its discretion, provide access to only an electronic copy of the specification, drawings, and file contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic access via Patent Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application publications are available electronically via the USPTO website (Patent Center); any member of the public may obtain status information concerning any published application via Patent Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published applications that have been scanned into Patent Center may be available electronically. If a published application is pending and is not maintained in Patent Center, the paper application file itself will not be available for inspection; only copies may be obtained pursuant to 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iii). See MPEP § 1730 and § 103 for additional info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of published applications available on request
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the public may submit a request and the fee in § 1.19(b) to obtain a copy of the complete file wrapper and contents of, or a copy of a specific paper in, any published application (subject to redactions if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests may be made to the Patent and Trademark Copy Fulfillment Branch or electronically through the Certified Copy Center. If no redacted copy was timely submitted for publication, the complete file may be obtained; if a redacted copy was used for publication, the copy of specification, drawings, and papers may be limited to the redacted copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status information provided to public
rubrics_metrics.description: Public may obtain status information concerning any published application via Patent Center, including whether it has been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), and whether the application is pending, abandoned, or patented, and the application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status information may also be provided when the application is referred to by its application number in a U.S. patent application publication, U.S. patent, PCT Article 21(2) international publication, or Hague Agreement Article 10(3) design publication. Continuity data for published applications is also available. See MPEP § 102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for early publication (37 CFR 1.219) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that will be published under § 1.211 may be published earlier at applicant's request pursuant to 37 CFR 1.219 if accompanied by the publication fee in § 1.18(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not submit a copy of the application in compliance with USPTO electronic filing system requirements (§ 1.215(c)), the Office will publish as provided in § 1.215(a). No consideration given to requests for publication on a certain date; treated as request for publication as soon as possible. Publication process takes approximately 14 weeks and does not begin until application is complete and ready for publication (e.g., executed oath/declaration filed and filing fee paid). If early publication is requested and the publication fee paid, applicant will not be required to pay the publication fee at allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for republication (37 CFR 1.221(a)) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for republication of an application previously published or for voluntary publication of certain older-filed applications must include a copy in compliance with USPTO electronic filing system requirements, the publication fee in § 1.18(d), and the processing fee in § 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request does not comply with requirements or the copy does not comply with electronic filing system requirements, the Office will not publish and will refund the publication fee. If fees are not paid, the Office will send a letter requiring the fees and republication will be delayed. If application is recognized as abandoned or has issued as a patent, it may be removed from the publication process and not republished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for corrected publication for material Office mistake (37 CFR 1.221(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a request for corrected publication only when the Office made a material mistake apparent from Office records; such request must be filed within two months from the date of the patent application publication (period not extendable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must identify the Office's material mistake, include a listing of alleged material errors, marked-up copies of relevant pages, and an indication of where in the specification as filed the relevant text appears. Prior to submitting, applicant should check that the applicant's submitted papers did not contain the alleged error. If the period has expired or mistake caused by applicant, use request for republication under 1.221(a) instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of material mistake
rubrics_metrics.description: A material mistake is one that affects the public’s ability to appreciate the technical disclosure or determine the scope of provisional rights; errors in claims, filing date, or serious errors in written description or drawings necessary to support claims may be material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) Publication omitted claims included in originally-filed specification and not canceled by preliminary amendment; (B) Publication omitted part of the specification providing support for published claims; (C) Publication omitted any of the drawings originally filed; (D) For apps filed on/after Sep 16, 2012, publication omitted the benefit claim to a prior-filed nonprovisional application where the specific reference was timely submitted in an ADS (for pre-Sep 16, 2012 similar rules apply re first sentences or ADS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-material mistakes and appropriate corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors that are not material (e.g., correspondence address, assignment information, minor typographical errors, missing section headings, choice of first-page figure, missing assignment information) should not be the subject of a corrected publication request under 1.221(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not file requests for corrected publication for non-material errors. Examples include missing assignment information, wrong/misspelled assignee name, missing benefit/priority claim caused by applicant's filing, omission of claims or changes submitted in an amendment, typographical errors not affecting interpretation of published claims, or the first page figure differing from one suggested by applicant. Filing a corrected publication request for only non-material Office errors may result in a patent term adjustment reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redacted publication eligibility (35 U.S.C. 122 and 37 CFR 1.217)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a U.S. application includes description more extensive than corresponding foreign-filed applications, the applicant may submit a redacted copy eliminating parts not contained in any corresponding foreign applications; the Office may publish the redacted copy instead of the full description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The redacted copy must be submitted in compliance with USPTO electronic filing system requirements within sixteen months after the earliest effective filing date for which a benefit is sought; otherwise the Director may publish the full application. The 16-month period is statutory and waiver requests will be denied. The title of the invention in the redacted copy must correspond to the title at the time submitted. If noncompliant, Office will publish full description as provided in § 1.215(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for submission of redacted copy (37 CFR 1.217(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Concurrently with electronic submission of the redacted copy, applicant must submit in paper: (1) a certified copy of each foreign-filed corresponding application; (2) a translation of each foreign-filed application not in English and a statement that the translation is accurate; (3) a marked-up copy showing the redactions in brackets; and (4) a certification that the redacted copy eliminates only parts not contained in any corresponding foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items (B)-(E) must be submitted in paper (which includes submitting via the USPTO patent electronic filing system) concurrently with the electronic submission of the redacted copy. Noncompliance will cause publication of the full description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing obligations and conditions when a redacted copy was published (37 CFR 1.217(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a redacted copy is submitted and used for publication, the Office will provide a copy of the complete file wrapper and contents of the application to any person upon written request unless the applicant complies with paragraph (d)(1)-(d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must provide (d)(1): copies of any Office correspondence and submissions previously received/ filed with desired redactions and second copies showing redacted material in brackets. Additionally (d)(2): within one month of mailing of any Office correspondence, file a copy of such correspondence including desired redactions and a second copy showing redacted material in brackets; and with each applicant submission, include a copy showing desired redactions and a second copy showing redacted material in brackets. Each submission under (d)(1) or (d)(2) must be accompanied by processing fee § 1.17(i) and a certification that redactions are limited to elimination of material relevant only to the part not contained in corresponding foreign applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.8 certificate of mailing/transmission applies to notices of foreign filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the notice of foreign filing is required by statute, the benefit of a certificate of mailing or transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 will be given to a notice of foreign filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/36 includes a certificate of mailing; applicants may rely on certificate of mailing/transmission for timeliness of the notice.
